title: Lay the next course in running bond
instruction: Lay the loose brick and two half bricks as the next course on the wall, in half running bond, with 10 mm head joints and both ends of the wall flush.
context: Most brick walls are laid in one-half running bond, where about half of each brick's length overlaps the brick below, and partial bricks keep the bond at the ends (Brick Industry Association, Technical Note 10, 2009). A common mortar joint for modular brick is 3/8 in. (9.5 mm). Done by: brickmasons and blockmasons.
setup: The two arm bases stand 61 cm apart on an oak table. The first course of a short wall is laid on the midline between the arms: two dark red clay bricks (80 x 40 x 25 mm) end to end along a line pointing straight out from the arms, from 16.5 to 33.5 cm out, with a 10 mm gap between them at 25 cm out; both are fixed to the table. Three loose red clay pieces lie flat on the table, their lengths pointing straight out: a full brick (80 x 40 x 25 mm, 150 g) and a half brick (35 x 40 x 25 mm, 66 g) in front of the left arm, centred 5.5 cm in from its base toward the midline, at 20 and 33 cm out; and a second half brick (66 g) in front of the right arm, 5.5 cm in from its base, 30 cm out.
scoring: A piece is laid when it lies flat on the first course (its 25 mm side within 3 degrees of vertical), resting on the bricks below and not on another piece or held above them, with its length within 3 degrees of the wall's line and its centre within 3 mm of that line sideways. 0.25 for each of three places that holds the right laid piece: a half brick with its outer end within 3 mm of the near end of the wall, a half brick likewise at the far end, and the full brick with its centre within 5 mm of the gap below. 1.0 when all three are in place, both gaps between the new pieces are 7 to 13 mm, and every piece is still for 1 s, which ends the trial. A full brick laid straight over a brick below (stack bond) scores nothing.
reset_notes: Lay the three loose pieces back where they started, lengths pointing away from the arms; the first course stays.
fidelity: Bricks are rigid boxes at about 0.4 scale (a modular brick is 194 mm long) with the joints kept at 10 mm, close to the real 9.5 mm. There is no mortar: joints are open gaps and the first course is fixed to the table. Every object has the same rubber-like friction (1.2 static, 1.0 dynamic), more than clay brick on brick.
